howItWorks.title:
From git push to live,
on your infrastructure.
howItWorks.subtitle: No agent on your servers, no black box. Here’s the exact path your code takes — and why your production machines never build.

steps.title: Connect
steps.body: Link a Git repo and pick a target — Openship Cloud or your own server over SSH. Nothing is installed on your box: no agent, no daemon, no dashboard.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: On every push the image builds on your machine (or in the cloud), runs your tests, and is tagged as an immutable, versioned artifact. Your production servers stay focused on serving.

steps.title: Ship
steps.body: The built image streams to the target over SSH and starts as a fresh container on an isolated private network — no exposed ports, no hand-written Docker or Compose.

steps.title: Route
steps.body: Your domains are wired through OpenResty with automatic Let's Encrypt SSL, then traffic swaps to the new container with zero downtime. The previous version stays ready for rollback.

steps.title: Operate
steps.body: Stream logs, watch metrics, and roll back to any previous version in one click — from the CLI, the web dashboard, the desktop app, or an AI agent over MCP.

openSource.headline:
Yours to run, fork,
and ship.
openSource.body: The dashboard, the CLI, the agents, the infrastructure adapters - all public, all readable, all auditable. Run it on a Raspberry Pi or a fleet. Contribute back when you want to.

mailServer.body: A real mail server on your own box - not a send-only API. Outbound relays through a trusted provider (Amazon SES or any SMTP) so mail lands with a warmed, high-reputation IP, while every mailbox, message, and byte stays on your server. One click sets up the domains, certificates, and SPF/DKIM/DMARC chain.

comparison.title:
Where Openship is
genuinely different.
comparison.subtitle: Git deploys, TLS, databases, backups, cron — every tool here has those, so they are not on this list. What is below is where the choice actually changes what you can do, and what it costs you to change your mind.

groups.title: Where it runs, and what stays on

rows.openship: Openship Cloud runs it, or self-host free on machines you own. One tool, one dashboard, and you can move either direction later.
rows.managed: They run it, and run it well - but managed-only. There is no version you can host yourself.
rows.selfhost: Their cloud hosts only the control panel. You still bring, run and pay for every server.

rows.feature: What has to stay switched on
rows.openship: A native Mac, Windows and Linux app. The control plane runs on your machine only while the app is open - no extra box to keep alive just to deploy.
rows.managed: No desktop app. Everything runs in their cloud, all the time.
rows.selfhost: No desktop app, and a control-plane server that has to stay up around the clock.

rows.openship: From the desktop app, your folder or repo goes straight to the machine that will run it. Nothing always-on sits in the middle holding your code.
rows.managed: Uploaded to their cloud and built there.
rows.selfhost: Lands on a long-lived control-plane box first - even when that box is your own.

rows.openship: A real mail server, set up for you: mailboxes, webmail, the SPF/DKIM/DMARC chain, and sending through SES or your own SMTP.
rows.managed: Not included. Add SendGrid, Resend or Postmark and pay per message.
rows.selfhost: No managed mail server - you run the image and wire up the DNS chain yourself.

rows.openship: Rate limits, country / IP / user-agent blocks and hotlink protection, set per route from the dashboard and applied without a reload.
rows.managed: Firewall and rate limiting exist, gated behind higher plans.
rows.selfhost: Possible by hand-writing proxy config; no country rules out of the box.

rows.feature: Who is actually hitting your app
rows.openship: Per-route traffic, country breakdown and a live request log, built in.
rows.managed: Strong analytics dashboards, capped or priced by plan.
rows.selfhost: Not included - bolt on Grafana, Plausible or an ELK stack.

rows.openship: Grant access down to a single project, start teammates at zero permissions, and export a record of every change - on every plan.
rows.managed: Broad team roles; audit trail and SSO on enterprise plans.
rows.selfhost: Broad team roles only, with little or no change history.

groups.title: Fits the setup you already have

rows.feature: Servers with things already on them
rows.openship: Point it at a server and it picks up the containers already running there. Nothing is rebuilt, nothing is restarted.
rows.managed: Nothing to pick up - you redeploy from source.
rows.selfhost: Cannot take on an app that is already running; you recreate each one by hand.

rows.openship: Carries on with your existing Traefik, nginx or Caddy on :80 and :443, and the switch is reversible in one step.
rows.managed: Not applicable - their edge, their rules.
rows.selfhost: Claims the proxy at install and expects to be the only thing on those ports.

rows.feature: Settings that live in your repo
rows.openship: openship.json describes build, env, domains, services and resources - reviewed in a pull request like the rest of your code.
rows.managed: vercel.json and netlify.toml do the same thing.
rows.selfhost: A Procfile or compose file, but domains, env and resources stay dashboard-only.

rows.openship: Move a running app with its volumes and certificates to another machine, then cut traffic over once it checks out.
rows.managed: Not applicable - you do not choose the machine.
rows.selfhost: Redeploy on the new box and copy the volumes across by hand.

rows.openship: On your own servers, removing a project deletes our record and nothing else. Containers, data and config keep serving traffic, and Openship can pick them back up later.
rows.managed: Nothing stays behind - the workload only ever existed in their cloud.
rows.selfhost: Deleting tears the app down, and none of them can re-adopt a running app afterwards.

comparison.foot: Compared against the shipping versions of each tool, July 2026. A dash means that tool genuinely matches Openship, or that the row does not apply to it. We would rather score a row even than invent a cross.

aboutPage.title: About
aboutPage.heroMeta: Built and maintained by the team at Oblien.

sections.title: What we build
paragraphs: Openship is a deployment platform you run yourself. Point it at a repository and it detects your stack, builds it, and ships it to any Linux server you own — with databases, domains, SSL, mail, and backups managed from one place.
The same platform comes as a CLI, a web dashboard, and a desktop app. Use whichever fits how you work; they all drive the same backend.

sections.title: Open source
paragraphs: Openship is open-source software under the Apache License 2.0. The dashboard, CLI, agents, and infrastructure adapters are all public and auditable on GitHub.

Every deployment is a standard Docker container with standard manifests — no proprietary formats, no lock-in. Run it on a Raspberry Pi, a single VPS, or a fleet, and move between providers whenever you like.

sections.title: Who's behind it
paragraphs: Openship is built and maintained by the team at Oblien (Oblien LLC), which builds cloud and developer infrastructure. It stays open under Apache 2.0 for everyone who deploys with it.
Openship Cloud — the managed option — is operated by Oblien, but the platform itself is yours to self-host, forever, at no cost.

sections.title: Get involved
paragraphs: Star or fork the project, open an issue, or send a pull request on GitHub. Bug reports and feature ideas are genuinely welcome — the docs and the platform improve fastest with them.
New here? Start with the documentation or install in one command.

aboutPage.footer: Want to reach us? Head to Contact.

privacyPage.title: Privacy
privacyPage.heroSubtitle: Openship collects only what is necessary to operate the platform, and your source remains on your infrastructure when self-hosted.
